findings.description: Privileged password stored in plaintext or reversible form, with no hashed secret
findings.remediation: Replace 'enable password' with 'enable secret <hash>' (IOS), use encrypted-password (JunOS) or ENC-hashed admin passwords (FortiOS). Hashed secrets cannot be read back from the configuration.

findings.description: AAA (Authentication, Authorization, Accounting) not configured
findings.remediation: Enable centralised AAA: 'aaa new-model' with RADIUS/TACACS+ method lists (IOS), 'authentication-order' with radius/tacplus servers (JunOS), or remote-auth admins backed by 'config user radius' (FortiOS).

findings.description: Telnet permitted for device management (cleartext credentials)
findings.remediation: Allow SSH only: 'transport input ssh' on all VTY lines (IOS), remove 'system services telnet' (JunOS), remove 'telnet' from interface allowaccess (FortiOS).

findings.description: SSH not enabled; no encrypted management access configured
findings.remediation: Enable SSHv2: 'ip ssh version 2' and 'crypto key generate rsa modulus 4096' (IOS), 'system services ssh' (JunOS), 'ssh' in allowaccess (FortiOS). Then restrict management to SSH.

findings.description: No login banner warns users before they authenticate
findings.remediation: Show a legal notice before login: 'banner login' (IOS, NX-OS, EOS, ASA), 'system login message' (JunOS), 'pre-login-banner' (FortiOS), login-banner (PAN-OS). Do not include device or site details in it.

findings.description: Management logins are accepted from any source address
findings.remediation: Limit who can reach the management plane: 'access-class <acl> in' on every VTY line (IOS/NX-OS), an input filter on lo0 (JunOS), 'trusthost' on every admin (FortiOS), 'ip access-group' under 'management ssh' (EOS), specific 'ssh'/'http' source networks (ASA), permitted-ip (PAN-OS).

findings.description: Repeated failed logins are not limited or locked out
findings.remediation: Slow down password guessing: 'login block-for' (IOS/NX-OS), 'aaa local authentication attempts max-fail' (IOS/ASA), 'system login retry-options' (JunOS), 'aaa authentication policy lockout' (EOS), admin-lockout failed-attempts (PAN-OS).

findings.description: Passwords stored in plaintext: password encryption is not enabled
findings.remediation: Store credentials hashed: 'secret' instead of 'password' (type 8/9 where supported) and 'service password-encryption' as a minimum on IOS; encrypted-password on JunOS; ENC admin passwords on FortiOS. Remove default credentials.

findings.description: No minimum length or complexity is enforced for local passwords
findings.remediation: Enforce a minimum length of 12 or more: 'security passwords min-length' (IOS), 'system login password minimum-length' (JunOS), 'config system password-policy' (FortiOS), 'password strength-check' (NX-OS), 'password-policy minimum-length' (ASA), password-complexity (PAN-OS).

findings.description: ACL contains unrestricted 'permit any any' (allows all traffic)
findings.remediation: Replace 'permit any any' entries (or all/all/ALL accept policies) with rules naming specific sources, destinations and services. End every ACL with an explicit deny and document each permit.

findings.description: Management interface has no inbound ACL applied
findings.remediation: Apply an inbound ACL/filter to every management interface that admits only known management hosts and the required protocols (SSH, SNMP, HTTPS).

findings.description: SNMPv1/v2c community string is a default or easily guessed value
findings.remediation: Replace default and short community strings with long random values (8+ characters, mixed classes). Migrate to SNMPv3 with SHA authentication and AES privacy, then remove v1/v2c communities.

findings.description: SNMPv1/v2c community string is a default or easily guessed value
findings.remediation: Replace default and short community strings with long random values (8+ characters, mixed classes). Migrate to SNMPv3 with SHA authentication and AES privacy, then remove v1/v2c communities.

findings.description: SNMP community is not restricted to known management hosts
findings.remediation: Bind every community to an ACL or client list of NMS addresses (IOS: 'snmp-server community <str> RO <acl>'; JunOS: 'clients'; FortiOS: community 'hosts').

findings.description: SNMP community is not restricted to known management hosts
findings.remediation: Bind every community to an ACL or client list of NMS addresses (IOS: 'snmp-server community <str> RO <acl>'; JunOS: 'clients'; FortiOS: community 'hosts').

findings.description: An SNMPv1/v2c community grants read-write access
findings.remediation: Remove read-write communities. If SNMP writes are needed, use an SNMPv3 user with authentication and privacy, limited by a view. Anyone who learns a read-write community can change the device.

findings.description: SNMP runs only as v1/v2c, which sends community strings and data unencrypted
findings.remediation: Configure SNMPv3 users with SHA authentication and AES privacy (authPriv), move the management station to them, then remove the v1/v2c communities.

findings.description: Plain-text HTTP management access is enabled
findings.remediation: Disable HTTP management ('no ip http server'; remove 'http' from web-management or allowaccess) and use HTTPS with TLS 1.2 or later and a valid certificate.

findings.description: CDP (Cisco Discovery Protocol) enabled globally
findings.remediation: Run 'no cdp run', or at least 'no cdp enable' on every external and untrusted interface. CDP discloses platform, version and addressing.

findings.description: TCP/UDP small servers enabled (echo, chargen, discard, daytime)
findings.remediation: Disable with 'no service tcp-small-servers' and 'no service udp-small-servers'. These services are obsolete and can be abused for amplification attacks.

findings.description: IP source routing is enabled (the sender can choose the path)
findings.remediation: Disable with 'no ip source-route'. Source-routed packets let an attacker steer traffic around filters and spoof trusted addresses.

findings.description: No remote syslog server configured
findings.remediation: Send logs to at least one remote collector ('logging host <ip>'; JunOS 'syslog host'; FortiOS 'log syslogd setting'). Centralised logs are required for security monitoring and incident response.

findings.description: Buffered (local) logging not enabled
findings.remediation: Enable a local log buffer ('logging buffered 65536 informational'; JunOS 'syslog file'; FortiOS memory/disk logging) as a fallback when the collector is unreachable.

findings.description: Log messages do not carry a date and time
findings.remediation: Stamp every message: 'service timestamps log datetime msec show-timezone' (IOS), 'logging timestamp' (ASA). Without timestamps, events cannot be ordered or matched across devices.

findings.description: NTP not configured; device clock may be unsynchronised
findings.remediation: Configure at least two trusted NTP servers. Accurate time is needed for log correlation, certificate validation and AAA event ordering.

findings.description: Interface is active but has no IP address or description assigned
findings.remediation: Shut down unused interfaces and describe every active one ('description <purpose>') so the inventory stays auditable.
